lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: You stood outside the office for a moment, transcript in hand. The sun was already lower in the sky, but it still caught the secretary’s window in a golden shimmer. You took a deep breath and stepped inside.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Every document you submitted was real. Your project was your own work. The certificate, earned through months of preparation. The motivational letter, written late at night under a weak desk lamp. You did not cut corners. You endured.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Weeks later, the results were posted. Your name stood tall on the list. With the scholarship came opportunities, handshakes, and the quiet pride of those who believed in you.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: People noticed the difference. You weren’t fast because you cheated; you were steady because you trained. When the work got harder, you didn’t panic—you adjusted. Integrity isn’t a medal. It’s a habit that pays interest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: You did it—the right way. And because of that, what comes next won’t break you.
